jobs.occupation: Senior scientific project coordinator
jobs.employer_name: NORCE RESEARCH AS AVD NATURVITENSKAP BERGEN
jobs.description:
About the position
The research group DARWIN (Data, AI, and Robotics) at the NORCE Technology and digital systems division is looking for a senior scientist in a permanent 100% position with the main role of initiating and coordinating large national and EU research proposals for the research group and scientifically coordinating them as well as designing novel concepts and solutions for AI and robot deployments. The group has strong technological professional expertise in data science, AI, computer vision, machine learning, robotics, mechatronics, cybernetics, computer engineering, visual sensing, visualization, advanced maintenance and smart instrumentation.

The place of work and employment can be any NORCE location. Travelling is expected.
Work tasks
The main tasks of the position will be to drive new large national and EU research possibilities, initiate and coordinate scientific proposal writing and applications, carry out the scientific coordination and management of projects within AI and robotics. Additional tasks include carrying out technological research and development projects in collaboration with industrial partners and research organization in Norway and in Europe, as well as collaborative projects with other groups and divisions within NORCE.
Required skills, expertise and experience
• 
Scientific background: minimum master’s degree in mechanical electronics, computer science and/or mechatronics or a related scientific area, with extensive knowledge in robotics, AI and perception systems.

• 
Documented experience of at least 10 years in national and EU research funding programs with a track record on initiating scientific large national and EU project applications, writing scientific national and EU project proposals and coordinating national and EU projects is particularly relevant to the position.

• 
Industrial experience is an advantage

• 
Being and having a certified project management with IPMA, PMP or similar

• 
Proficiency in English. Knowledge of the Norwegian language is an advantage.

• 
Good team working skills while being proactive.

• 
Excellent communication and organizational skills.
We offer
• 
A good and professionally challenging working environment

• 
Exciting interdisciplinary projects together with national and international partners

• 
A nationwide network of researchers in NORCE

• 
Exciting, varied and flexible workday

• 
Interdisciplinary work in teams with experts in other fields

• 
Great opportunities for professional and personal development in a new and expansive competence environment

• 
A social and creative work environment where you have a large influence on your own workday

• 
Good pension and insurance schemes, good welfare schemes and competitive wages
How to apply
Please upload your application by pressing the application button. Your application should be written in English and must include the following:

• 
CV

• 
A cover letter with a description of your professional qualifications and motivation to apply for the position

• 
Names and contact information of two references

• 
Copy of diplomas, transcripts and relevant certificates from your higher education
Application deadline: 3 January 2027
Further information about the position can be obtained by contacting research leader Nabil Belbachir, tel. 401 08 137, or nabe@norceresearch.no.

At NORCE, we are committed to ensuring diversity, equity and inclusion. We encourage all qualified individuals to apply for available positions regardless of gender, age, disability, or ethnic background.

Candidates are expected to openly offer relevant information about themselves during the recruitment process. Furthermore, one can expect background checks to be conducted on candidates in the final phase of the recruitment process. NORCE uses external actors to carry out such background checks.

NORCE is subject to the Security Act and there are strict requirements for our employees to have a security-conscious behavior. For this position, you must satisfy the security clearance requirements for SECRET/NATO SECRET.

Further information about security clearance can be found on the National Security Authority's (NSM) website: NSM.no

Vil du bruke kunnskapen din til noe som virkelig betyr noe? I NORCE blir du med på et lag som leverer viktig forskning og bærekraftige løsninger – regionalt, nasjonalt og globalt.

Vi er et av Norges største forskningsinstitutter, med over 800 ansatte i 10 byer langs Norges kyst. Hos oss er kunnskap, nytenkning og godt samarbeid nøkkelen til å lykkes.

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Translational Research
jobs.description:
The position
Do you want to contribute to research about non-coding RNAs in sperm health and infertility?

A PhD position is available at the Department of Clinical Medicine, Faculty of Health Sciences in the Translational Vascular Research group, working on the project ´Developmental non-coding RNA signatures of sperm health and infertility´

The Translational Vascular Research group includes both basic scientists and clinicians. We perform research spanning across disciplines, from the analysis of patient samples to laboratory based investigation of cell behaviour. Parts of our research group are based at Karolinska Institute/KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden, with the opportunity for close collaborations with these institutes.The fertility department at the Women’s clinic at the University Hospital of North Norway (UNN) is a collaboration partner and will contribute with expertise in andrology and analysis of semen samples.

The position is for a period of four years. The nominal length of the PhD program is three years. The fourth year is distributed as 25% each year and will consist of teaching and other duties for the Department of Clinical Medicine. The objective of the position is to complete research training to the level of a doctoral degree. Admission to a PhD programme is a prerequisite for employment, and the programme period starts on commencement of the position. 

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.
The project 
Male infertility is an increasing global health concern, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying impaired sperm function remain poorly understood. Previously, our group identified more than 2,000 testis-enriched non-coding RNAs and characterised their expression across germ-cell development. In this project, you will investigate which of these non-coding RNAs persist into mature sperm and whether their expression is associated with sperm quality and fertility. In collaboration with the fertility clinic atthe University Hospital of North Norway (UNN), you will analyse sperm samples from fertility patients and healthy donors. Using sperm phenotyping, cell sorting and RNA sequencing, you will examine differences in non-coding RNA expression between sperm populations with different functional characteristics, including motility and morphology. Selected transcripts will also be investigated in matched testicular tissue using imaging and in situ hybridisation to study their expression during germcell development. By integrating molecular and clinical data, the project aims to identify non-coding RNA signatures associated with sperm health and their potential as biomarkers of male fertility.
 
You must submit a cover letter explaining your motivation and research interests. 
Contact
For further information about the position, please contact: 

Professor Lynn Butler 

• phone: +47 776 25 104
• email: lynn.m.butler@uit.noQualifications
Required Professional Qualifications

• A Candidate Medicine, or a Master’s degree in biological sciences . If you are near completion of your Master’s degree, you may still apply and submit a draft version of the thesis. You must document completion of your degree before commencement in the position.
• Documented fluency in English.
Preferred Qualifications, but not required:

• Working knowledge of Norwegian or a Scandinavian language
• Prior experience with cell culture-based laboratory projects, bioinformatics is beneficial. The candidate must be flexible and keen to work as part of a larger team.
Applicants must document fluency of in English and be able to work in an international environment. Nordic applicants can document their English capabilities by attaching their high school diploma. Working knowledge of Norwegian or a Scandinavian language is also beneficial.

In the assessment, the emphasis is on the applicant's potential to complete a research education based on the master's thesis or equivalent, and any other scientific work. In addition, professional experience and other experience of significance for the completion of the doctoral programme will be taken into consideration.

Required Personal Qualifications

• An enthusiasm for research and learning
• Ability to work independently and as part of a larger team
• Willingness to collaborate with others During the assessment, emphasis will be put on your potential, motivation and personal suitability for the position.
As many people as possible should have the opportunity to undertake organized research training. If you already hold a PhD or have equivalent competence, we will not appoint you to this position.
Admission to the PhD programme 
For employment in the PhD position, you must be qualified for admission to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Health Sciences and participate in organized doctoral studies within the employment period.

Admission normally requires:  

• A bachelor's degree of 180 ECTS and a master's degree of 120 ECTS, or an integrated master's degree of 300 ECTS. 
• A master's thesis with a scope corresponding to at least 30 ECTS for a master's degree of 120 ECTS. 
• A master's thesis with a scope corresponding to at least 20 ECTS for an integrated master's degree of 300 ECTS. 
 
 
Applicants must have a grade of C or better on the master's thesis and have a grade point average of C or better for the master's degree. A more detailed description of admission requirements can be found here.

If you are employed in the position, you will be provisionally admitted to the PhD programme. Application for final admission must be submitted no later than two months after taking up the position. 

Applicants with a foreign education will be subjected to an evaluation of whether the educational background is equal to Norwegian higher education, following national guidelines from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills. Depending on which country the education is from, one or two additional years of university education may be required to fulfil admission requirements, e.g. a 4-year bachelor's degree and a 2-year master's degree. UiT normally accepts higher education from countries that are part of the Lisbon Recognition Convention.
Inclusion and diversity
UiT The Arctic University of Norway is working actively to promote equality, gender balance and diversity among employees and students, and to create an inclusive and safe working environment. We believe that inclusion and diversity are a strength, and we want employees with different competencies, professional experience, life experience and perspectives.

If you have a disability, a gap in your CV or immigrant background, we encourage you to tick the box for this in your application. If there are qualified applicants, we invite at least one in each group for an interview. If you get the job, we will adapt the working conditions if you need it. Apart from selecting the right candidates, we will only use the information for anonymous statistics.
We offer
• Involvement in an interesting research project 
• Good career opportunities 
• A good academic environment with dedicated colleagues  
• Flexible working hours and a state collective pay agreement  
• Pension scheme through the state pension fund 
• PhD Fellows are normally given a salary of 580 000 NOK/year with a 3% yearly increase
Norwegian health policy aims to ensure that everyone, irrespective of their personal finances and where they live, has access to good health and care services of equal standard. As an employee you will become member of the National Insurance Scheme which also include health care services.

More practical information about working and living in Norway can be found here: https://uit.no/staffmobility
Application 
Please note that the application will only be assessed based on the information submitted by the application deadline via Jobbnorge. It is therefore important that you include all necessary documents demonstrating your qualifications for the position.

Your application must include: 

• Cover letter explaining your motivation and research interests
• CV
• Official diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degree in the original language 
• Official transcripts of grades/academic record for Bachelor's and Master's degree in the original language
• Official translation of diplomas and transcripts of records (ToR) to English or a Scandinavian language, if applicable
• Explanation of the grading system for foreign education (Diploma Supplement if available)
• Documentation of English proficiency
• References with contact information
• Master’s thesis, and any other academic works
Qualification with a master’s degree is required before commencement in the position. If you are near completion of your master’s degree, you may still apply and submit a draft version of the thesis and a statement from your supervisor or institution indicating when the degree will be obtained. You must still submit your transcript of grades for the master’s degree with your application.

All documentation to be considered must be in a Scandinavian language or English. If English proficiency is not documented in the application, it must be documented before starting in the position. 
Assessment 
The applicants will be assessed by an expert committee. The committee's mandate is to undertake an assessment of the applicants' qualifications based on the written material presented by the applicants, and the detailed description draw up for the position. A copy of the assessment report will be sent to all applicants. 

The applicants who are assessed as best qualified will be called to an interview. The interview should among other things, aim to clarify the applicant’s motivation and personal suitability for the position. 
General information 
The appointment is made in accordance with State regulations and guidelines at UiT. At our website, you will find more information for applicants.

Remuneration for the position of PhD Fellow is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1017. A compulsory contribution of 2 % to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted. You will become a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund, which gives you many benefits in addition to a lifelong pension: You may be entitled to financial support if you become ill or disabled, your family may be entitled to financial support when you die, you become insured against occupational injury or occupational disease, and you can get good terms on a mortgage. Read more about your employee benefits at: spk.no.
 
A shorter period of appointment may be decided when the PhD Fellow has already completed parts of their research training programme or when the appointment is based on a previous qualifying position PhD Fellow, research assistant, or the like in such a way that the total time used for research training amounts to three years. 

We process personal data given in an application or CV in accordance with the Personal Data Act (Offentleglova). According to the Personal Data Act information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure. You will receive advance notification in the event of such publication, if you have requested non-disclosure.

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Experimental Microfluidics and Flotation
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The PHASE Group at the Department of Chemical Engineering at NTNU has a vacant PhD position in which experimental techniques in microfluidics and lab-scale flotation will be used to investigate the recovery of solid mineral particles via bubble formation. The work is part of the project MINBUBBLE funded by the Det Norske Veritas Foundation. The PhD candidate will collaborate with researchers within the PHASE group and at KTH Royal Institute of Technology who will investigate the system with computational methods.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
MINBUBBLE: Mineral-Driven Bubble Nucleation for Critical Raw Materials Recovery in Flotation tackles fundamental scientific questions in how mineral particles can be better recovered. Sustainable access to critical raw materials is an environmental and geopolitical imperative, and current mineral extraction and refining methods are inadequate to meet these demands. Specifically, the recovery of minerals using froth flotation struggles to capture the finest fraction of particles due to insufficient attachment of particles to the bubbles. Worsening quality of ores also means that finer fractions are more commonly encountered in operations. 

To recover the fines, one solution may be to abruptly decrease the pressure of the system and initiate bubble formation directly on the mineral particle surfaces. This process is known as dissolved gas flotation (DGF), but it is not used in industrial mineral recovery due to a persistent lack of knowledge regarding the physicochemical processes that drive DGF. At NTNU, experimental work using microfluidics and a lab-scale flotation setup is planned to provide new data and understanding of the generation of bubbles in the presence of different minerals and varying water properties. Together, the experimental and computational results will establish the viability of DGF for extracting critical raw materials as a new, sustainable approach.

The project MINBUBBLE is led by Associate Professor Nadia Shardt in collaboration with Professor Gisle Øye at NTNU and Assistant Professor Shahab Mirjalili at KTH. It is funded under the call topic “Critical Raw Materials” by the Det Norske Veritas Foundation.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until a doctorate is obtained.
• Carry out research of high quality within the framework described above.
• Contribute with academic publications complying with open science principles and popular science dissemination.
• Participate in the PHASE research group at the Department of Chemical Engineering.
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions.
• Teaching and teaching assistant duties may be required during the employment period.  
Changes to your work duties may occur after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemistry, or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than the start date of the position.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• You must have excellent written and oral English language skills.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Experience with operating gas flotation equipment.
• Experience with particle characterization techniques.
• Knowledge of colloid and interfacial science.
• Experience with image processing and object detection.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian.Personal characteristics
• To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 
• Demonstrated interest and ability to work in a collaborative setting.
• Proactive mindset for conducting innovative research.
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject.
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions.
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• An exciting job with an important mission in society.
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment.
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period.
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues.
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project.
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU.
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK).
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2).
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work with a preferred start date in May 2027, but no later than August 2027.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Chemical Engineering within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment.

The position is conditional on external funding.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees.
• CV .
• Copy of Master's thesis. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page).
• Possibly publications etc. other relevant research work.
• Possibly certificates.
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees.
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position  - in the Oral Physiology and Cancer Research Group (OPCG)
jobs.description:
About the position 
A PhD research fellowship is available in the Oral Physiology and Cancer Research Group (OPCG) at the Institute of Oral biology, Faculty of Dentistry, the University of Oslo. One of our group’s major interests is the study of how extracellular vesicles from cancer cells affect various normal cells, both in the immediate vicinity of the tumor and at a distance, changing their phenotype to support the growing tumor mass. In the proposed project, we aim to investigate the effect of extracellular vesicles from oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) on the function of normal cells, including endothelial cells. 
 
The candidate will apply various experimental methods to assess whether the normal phenotype changes towards a tumor-supporting one upon OSCC-derived extracellular vesicle exposure. Such alterations may include increased proliferation, modifications of intracellular Ca2+ signalling pathways, shifts in the metabolic profile and more.     
More about the position
The main purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree. 

Project title: “Tumor-host interaction in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC)”

This is a 100% full-time, three-year PhD Research Fellowship position. The successful candidate is expected to produce three scientific papers and a doctoral thesis. The place of work is Oslo, Norway.
More about the fellowship
Admission to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Dentistry is a prerequisite for taking up the position. The candidate is expected to complete the project within the fellowship period. A final plan for the research training must be approved and formalised no later than three months after the start of the position.

The main supervisor will be Professor Trude Marie Haug - Institute of Oral Biology
Qualification requirements
Mandatory requirements

• Applicants must hold a Master’s degree equivalent to a Norwegian master’s degree in molecular biology, cell biology, dentistry or in another field relevant to the research project.
• The Master’s thesis must have a grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system.
• A good level of written and oral communication skills in English is required.
• English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements: https://www.odont.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/supplementary-rules.html
• Publications in international peer-reviewed scientific journals will be advantageous but not required
Experience in the following methods will be advantageous:

• Cell culturing
• Standard molecular biological techniques and immunohistochemistry
• Analysis of -omics data
• Intracellular Ca2+ imagingPersonal skills:
• Ability to work independently and in an interdisciplinary scientific environment
• Self-motivation, creativity, genuine curiosity about the subject, work discipline, professional ethics, and ambition
• Strong practical and analytical skills
• Good social and collaboration skills
We need different perspectives in our work

Applicants with an immigrant background, a disability or gaps in their CV are encouraged to indicate this in the application portal. UiO invites at least one qualified applicant from each of these groups to interview in accordance with applicable state-sector procedures.Why should you choose us?
• A clearly defined and fully funded three-year PhD project with established core infrastructure.
• Dedicated supervision and research-training.
• An interdisciplinary and internationally connected research environment at the Faculty of Dentistry.
• A workplace with good development and career opportunities, good welfare schemes and up to 1.5 hours per week of exercise during working hours.(Good welfare schemes)
• Membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (Statens Pensjonskasse), with beneficial pension, mortgage and insurance arrangements.

Read more about the benefits of working in the public sector at Employer Portal.
How to apply
Your application must include:

jobs.description:
Location: Oslo, Norway
About the role
At Schibsted, reliable IT services are essential to helping our employees do their best work.

We are looking for an IT Service Desk Technician to join our Service Desk team in Oslo, providing high-quality technical support to employees across our organisation, primarily in Norway and Sweden.

Our Service Desk is more than a traditional first-line support function. We resolve approximately 80% of all incoming IT requests and incidents within the team, which means you will have the opportunity to work with a wide range of technical challenges, take ownership of issues and develop your troubleshooting skills.

You will work in an international environment where customer satisfaction, technical expertise and continuous improvement are key priorities. Our IT operations follow IT Service Management (ITSM) principles and ITIL practices, with a strong focus on efficient problem-solving, knowledge sharing and improving the employee IT experience.
Your responsibilities
As an IT Service Desk Technician, your main responsibilities will include:

• 
Deliver high-quality IT support: Provide professional, friendly and solution-oriented technical support to employees through phone, email and other support channels.

• 
Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues: Investigate and resolve incidents involving computers, operating systems, applications, user accounts, access and other workplace technologies.

• 
Own incidents and service requests: Register, prioritise, investigate, document and follow up on cases in our ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Halo), taking responsibility for driving issues towards resolution.

• 
Ensure a great user experience: Communicate clearly with users, provide regular updates and manage expectations throughout the support process.

• 
Drive efficient resolution and knowledge sharing: Contribute to our high resolution rate by developing technical knowledge, documenting solutions and supporting a shift-left approach.

• 
Collaborate and continuously improve: Work closely with colleagues and other IT teams to resolve complex issues and improve processes related to Incident, Problem, Change and Knowledge Management.

• 
Manage IT equipment and suppliers: Support ordering, inventory management and distribution of IT equipment and accessories, including coordination with external suppliers.
What we're looking for
We are looking for someone who enjoys solving technical challenges, takes ownership of problems and genuinely likes helping people.

You are curious about technology, comfortable investigating unfamiliar issues and motivated by finding solutions rather than simply passing problems on to someone else.

You enjoy working in an environment where priorities can change quickly and where teamwork, knowledge sharing and customer satisfaction are essential.
Skills and knowledge
To succeed in this role, we believe you have:

• 
A good understanding of computers, operating systems, software and common workplace IT technologies.

• 
The ability to troubleshoot technical issues in a structured and logical way.

• 
Familiarity with, or an interest in learning, technologies such as Windows, macOS, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and Microsoft Entra ID.

• 
An understanding of the importance of documenting incidents, solutions and technical information.

• 
The ability to communicate technical information clearly to users with different levels of IT knowledge.

• 
Professional proficiency in Norwegian or Swedish, as well as English, both written and spoken.
Nice to have
The following qualifications are an advantage, but not essential:

• 
Previous experience working in an IT Service Desk, IT Support or similar technical support role.

• 
Around two years of relevant technical experience or education.

• 
Experience working with ITSM platforms such as ServiceNow or Halo.

• 
Knowledge of ITIL principles and IT Service Management processes.

• 
Relevant IT certifications or technical training.

• 
Experience with IT equipment management, inventory control or supplier coordination.

• 
Experience with AI tools and technologies, particularly using AI to improve IT support, automate tasks, enhance troubleshooting or streamline workflows.

We value practical skills, curiosity and a willingness to learn. You do not need to meet every preferred qualification to be considered for the role.
Who you are
We believe the following qualities will help you succeed:

• 
Customer oriented: You enjoy helping others, understand their needs and take pride in delivering excellent service.

• 
Problem-solving: You approach technical challenges with curiosity, persistence and a structured mindset, taking responsibility for finding solutions.

• 
Communication: You explain technical issues clearly, listen actively and keep users informed throughout the support process.

• 
Adaptable: You are comfortable handling changing priorities, learning new technologies and working in a dynamic IT environment.

• 
Collaborative: You enjoy sharing knowledge, supporting colleagues and contributing to a positive and supportive team environment.
Why join us?
You will join a Service Desk team in Oslo where technical problem-solving, collaboration and high-quality service go hand in hand.

Unlike traditional first-line support roles, our team handles and resolves the majority of incoming IT issues, giving you the opportunity to work with a broad range of technologies and technical challenges.

You will support colleagues across Norway and Sweden, work with modern workplace technologies and contribute to continuously improving how IT services are delivered.

We believe great IT support is about more than fixing technical problems. It is about taking ownership, building trust and making people's working lives easier.

Skilled Painters - Bergen

Skuteviken Personell AS is seeking skilled and independent painters for projects in Bergen and the surrounding area.

As a painter, you will work with both interior and exterior painting on renovation and new-build projects. Typical tasks include surface preparation such as filling, sanding, and smoothing of walls and ceilings, application of paint using roller, brush, and preferably spray equipment, as well as finishing work with a strong focus on quality and precision.

We are looking for painters who take pride in high-quality workmanship and can work efficiently both independently and as part of a team.

We offer:

• 

Competitive salary: NOK 270 -290 per hour (depending on experience)

• 

Permanent employment

• 

Exciting and varied work tasks (both interior and exterior)

• 

Free professional tools and work clothes

• 

Housing in company apartments if needed

• 

Supportive and service-oriented administration

Requirements:

• 

Minimum 3 years' professional painting experience

• 

Strong skills in both exterior and interior paintwork

• 

Knowledge of Norwegian painting methods, especially interior groundwork and plastering

• 

Ability to follow and understand technical instructions and building methods

• 

Scandinavian or English language skills (professional competence is most important)

Personal qualities:

• 

High work ethic

• 

Reliable and punctual

• 

Structured and able to plan the workday effectively

Interested?

Please send your CV and application as soon as possible. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis.
